extra.motion: Locked-off head-on shot of the three steel stalls, camera fixed at chest height. For two seconds nothing happens: fine rain drifts down, the dark bay SHARES flicks an ear, the grey HOUSES shifts its weight, the chestnut WAGES on the right blinks. Then all three front gates bang open outward at the same instant, the white cloths swinging away with them. SHARES and HOUSES lunge forward out of their stalls, jockeys crouching low; WAGES stays exactly where it is, calm, head steady. Sound: soft rain, a sharp metallic clang of the gates, a thud of hooves on wet turf, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

The camera stays square to the stalls and creeps very slowly closer through the drizzle, building tension. The horses stand tight: bridles jingle, a jockey's gloved hand tightens on the reins, breath steams from the grey's nostrils. At about three seconds the three front gates fly open together with a loud spring-loaded crash and swing toward the lens. The two horses on the left and centre burst forward at once, flinging up wet grass; the chestnut on the right simply watches them go. Sound: rain patter, creak of steel, the crash of the gates, a rush of hooves, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

Static camera inside the commentary booth. The masked man in the tweed jacket holds the binoculars to the mask with his gloved hand, quite still, as raindrops run down the glass. Then he leans slowly forward toward the window, elbows lifting, and his head turns smoothly to the right as he tracks the race moving across the course below. His mask, headset, gloves, shirt and tie stay exactly as they are. The small monitor flickers green. Sound: rain tapping on the glass, a faint distant roar and drumming hooves from the course, the hum of the monitor, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

A slow, gentle push-in from behind the desk toward the masked commentator. He keeps the binoculars pressed to his mask; on the start he gives a small, sudden lean forward, shoulders tensing, then follows the runners with steady little turns of the head from left to right. His free gloved hand rises briefly to steady the binoculars with both hands. Rain streaks the window and the green course stretches away behind. Mask, gloves and tweed stay exactly as in the first frame. Sound: rain on glass, papers rustling, a distant crowd swell and hooves, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

Low head-on camera tracking backward as SHARES, the dark bay on the left, and HOUSES, the grey on the right, gallop straight at the lens side by side, jockeys crouched, clods of wet turf and mud spraying from their hooves. The camera keeps them filling the frame for the whole clip. Behind them, on the right, the chestnut WAGES stays inside its shut stall, head over the gate, calmly watching them leave and growing smaller. Cloth words stay exactly as they are. Sound: thundering hooves, horses blowing hard, rain, a rising crowd roar far off, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

The camera is fixed on the ground, low and still, as the two runners charge toward it: the dark bay SHARES and the grey HOUSES stretch into full gallop, legs reaching, manes flying, mud kicking up in slow heavy arcs. They thunder past either side of the lens and out of frame by six seconds, leaving the shot open on the stalls, where the chestnut WAGES stands alone behind its closed gate, chewing, ears relaxed. Rain keeps falling. Sound: hooves pounding and fading away, flying turf, rain, then quiet with a faint far-off crowd, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

Locked-off camera facing the chestnut WAGES behind its shut barred gate. The horse chews a mouthful of hay slowly and contentedly, wisps waggling, ears soft, completely unhurried. As it keeps chewing, time passes like a time-lapse: grey clouds race overhead, the daylight dims to blue dusk, the empty grandstand fades into dark, then pale dawn light returns, rain comes and goes on the steel bars, and the hay pile in front shrinks. The horse stays in the same spot the whole time, still chewing. Sound: steady munching, rain on metal, wind, a lone bird at dawn, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

A very slow push-in toward the chestnut horse's face through the gate bars. WAGES chews hay in long, lazy circles, blinks, lowers its head to pull another mouthful from the pile, then lifts it again, totally at ease. Around it the light changes in long sweeps: grey afternoon, a wash of orange evening, night with a faint floodlight glow, then flat morning grey, puddles on the turf behind filling and drying. The cloth reading WAGES and the closed gate stay exactly as they are. Sound: unhurried chewing, dripping rain, wind across the empty course, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

Handheld camera in the crowded winners' enclosure. The man in the camel coat tips the champagne bottle and a foaming spray pours over the laughing older man's flat cap, running down his waxed jacket. The woman in the hat kisses the grey horse's nose again; the horse flicks an ear, rosette fluttering, HOUSES on its rug unchanged. Hands clink flutes in the foreground, bubbles spilling. Behind, the packed grandstand waves and cheers under drizzle. Sound: cheering, laughter, glasses chinking, a champagne fizz, rain, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

The camera drifts slowly backward and slightly up, revealing more of the jostling celebration around the grey winner. The man in the camel coat shakes the bottle hard and a jet of champagne arcs across the group, catching the light; the older man throws his head back laughing, soaked. Glasses are raised high and clinked, the woman pats the grey's neck, the red and blue rosette bobs, and the HOUSES rug stays readable. Umbrellas and arms wave in the stands behind. Sound: a crowd roar, laughter, applause, pops and fizzing, rain, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

Wide static shot. The chestnut WAGES, rider aboard, trots steadily from left to right through the shallow floodwater on the empty course, each hoof splashing up small fans of water, its reflection rippling below. Heavy rain sweeps across in grey curtains in front of the deserted grandstand; the old stalls sit abandoned in the grass behind. The horse never hurries, just keeps an even, patient trot toward the right edge of frame. Sound: hard rain, sloshing hooves, wind, a creak of tack, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

The camera pans slowly left to right, keeping pace with the chestnut WAGES as it trots alone through the flooded straight, rider sitting quietly, water splashing knee-high with every stride. Rain hammers the puddles into rings; the vast empty stand looms grey and silent, rows of seats gleaming wet. The horse gives a little shake of its head and carries on, steady and alone, the white rail running beside it. Sound: steady downpour, splashing hooves, a distant gust, no crowd, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

High, wide, locked-off view down the misty straight. The long line of horses waits at the stalls in a single row, silks bright against the grass, a few heads bobbing. After a short pause every gate opens at once and the whole field moves off together, perfectly level, a single straight line of horses galloping up the wide green track toward the misty bend, nobody ahead and nobody behind. Spray rises from the wet turf. Sound: one crisp clang along the whole row, a rumble of many hooves, light rain, a distant cheer, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.

From the high vantage the camera tilts gently and begins to glide forward over the course. The row of horses stands ready at the long stalls; then all the front gates fly open in the same instant and every horse leaps out together, the field staying in one even line as it gallops along the striped turf between the white rails, coloured caps level across the whole width. The camera follows the line as it rolls away into the drifting fog. Sound: a single metal crash, a wave of hooves on soft ground, rain, a far-off crowd roar, no talking. Real-looking footage of an English racecourse on a grey, wet day. Thanks.
